sources.title: Television: The Public Sphere and National Identity
sources.source_location: Price frames television through public sphere, regulation, democratic values and national identity; this is a conceptual framework, not empirical proof of a programme effect.

sources.title: National and Post-National Identity
sources.source_location: The chapter treats national identity as historically and politically organised myths, ideas and narratives and links state-media relations to public sphere and identity claims.

sources.title: Vedtekter og NRK-plakaten
sources.source_location: The statutes separately state democratic mission, public conversation, Norwegian and Sámi identity and culture, religion/worldview diversity, all age groups, children's rights and balanced election coverage.

sources.title: Allmennkringkastingsrapporten 2025 – NRK
sources.source_location: The 2026 regulatory report evaluates NRK's 2025 fulfilment of democratic, social and cultural obligations, including debate, election coverage, children and youth and climate/nature blind spots.

sources.title: PSM Governance: Protecting the institutional and editorial independence of PSM
sources.source_location: The guidance treats editorial and institutional independence as a governance condition for public-service media and a democratic public forum, not as audience-effect evidence.

sources.title: Democracy and Public Service Media
sources.source_location: The report positions free and independent media and public-service media within democratic information infrastructure; it supports institutional analysis rather than causal audience claims.

sources.title: Public Service Values, Editorial Principles and Guidelines
sources.source_location: The EBU record identifies public-service values including independence; stated principles remain distinct from measured performance, reception or effect.

sources.title: The Oxford Handbook of Children's Film
sources.source_location: The handbook separates definitions of children's film, representations of childhood and growing up, national identity and audience engagement.

sources.title: Growing Up on Scandinavian Screens
sources.source_location: The chapter identifies historical strands in Danish, Norwegian and Swedish youth film and changing pedagogical, aesthetic and commercial ideas of youth cinema.

sources.title: Growing up and growing old with television: peripheral viewers and the centrality of care
sources.source_location: The article connects television form and care to the very young and very old while challenging normative models of growing up, ageing and spectatorship.

sources.title: Boyhood
sources.source_location: The BFI record anchors Richard Linklater's Boyhood as a concrete work for life-course analysis rather than a generalized claim about youth.

sources.publisher: British Film Institute / Sight and Sound
sources.title: The Father review: depiction of mental deterioration
sources.source_location: The review analyses dementia, temporal dislocation and subjective form in The Father without treating disease representation as evidence about older audiences.

sources.title: Metropolis
sources.source_location: The BFI record identifies Metropolis as a vertically divided megacity where workers sustain a ruling elite, linking built space and social hierarchy.

sources.publisher: British Film Institute / Sight and Sound
sources.title: Strife and the city: urban space and the essay film
sources.source_location: The essay surveys how essay films use urban space to interrogate received ideology and power, with named works and formal strategies.

sources.title: City of God
sources.source_location: The BFI record anchors City of God as a concrete urban film case; social claims still require contextual evidence rather than location inference.

sources.title: The Climate of Ecocinema
sources.source_location: The reference article maps ecocinema across fiction, documentary, animation, transnational cinema and climate fiction and distinguishes several critical approaches.

sources.title: Documentary as Ecocinema: Form, Ethics, and Environmental Justice
sources.source_location: The chapter connects documentary form and ethics to environmental justice, supporting formal analysis without presuming educational or behavioural impact.

sources.title: From FernGully to Farthing Wood: the 90s green wave of eco animations
sources.source_location: The BFI analysis situates Princess Mononoke within 1990s environmental animation and supplies a concrete case for complex human/nonhuman conflict.

sources.title: Panic on the streets of London: filming The Day the Earth Caught Fire
sources.source_location: The BFI account documents displaced climate zones, London setting and realist production choices, supporting representation and form claims rather than audience effects.

sources.publisher: Yale Program on Climate Change Communication
sources.title: Before and After The Day After Tomorrow: A U.S. Study of Climate Change Risk Perception
sources.source_location: The peer-reviewed pre/post study directly measures changes among moviegoers in climate-risk perception and intentions, providing a separate evidentiary basis for effect claims.

sources.title: Accented Cinema: The Context of Nollywood
sources.source_location: The chapter uses Ije: The Journey to examine exile, migration, diaspora and Nollywood's transnational dimensions.

sources.title: Migrations and Representations: The Cinema of Griot Dani Kouyaté
sources.source_location: The chapter analyses migration as physical and perceptual movement across four features and links migrant sensibility to changing vision and narrative position.

sources.title: Dirty Pretty Things
sources.source_location: The BFI record anchors Dirty Pretty Things as a named work; migration, labour and identity claims require separate contextual evidence.

sources.title: Waving the Flag: Constructing a National Cinema in Britain
sources.source_location: Higson surveys theories and institutional-cultural strategies of national cinema, allowing national screen culture to be analysed as constructed rather than assumed coherent.

sources.title: Your Britain on Film
sources.source_location: The BFI National Archive project presents 120 years of British lives, places, home movies, documentary and news footage while surfacing hidden histories and forgotten stories.

sources.title: Combining Methods in a Longitudinal Study of Religion in the Media
sources.source_location: The chapter documents coded religion references in a defined newspaper and terrestrial-TV sample followed by qualitative analysis, separating corpus pattern from interpretation.

sources.title: Islamic Prayer in Mainstream US Television and Film
sources.source_location: The chapter analyses mainstream US screen depictions of Islamic prayer and recurring representational patterns; it does not establish beliefs or reception among Muslim audiences.

sources.title: US Muslims’ Creative Approaches to Prayer on the Big and Small Screen
sources.source_location: The chapter examines Muslim-produced American screen portrayals of prayer, enabling comparison of creator position, convention and representation without reducing religion to visual markers.
